Generics

Generic functions

Type parameters go in angle brackets after the name.

fn identitas<T>(T datum) → T {
    return datum
}

main {
    print identitas("Marcus")
    print identitas(42)
}

The same function serves both calls. T is fixed per call site, not erased to a dynamic value.

Generic with a union return

Type parameters compose with unions, which is how "maybe nothing" is expressed generically.

fn primum<T>(list<T> res) → T ∪ null {
    if res.length() ≡ 0 then return null
    return res[0]
}

main {
    print primum([1, 2, 3])
}

Generic containers

The built-in collections are generic already.

main {
    const list<string> nomina ← ["Marcus", "Julia"]
    const map<string, int> aetates ← { "Marcus": 30 }
    print nomina, aetates
}

Records

genus declares a record type with type-first fields.

class Persona {
    string nomen
    int aetas
}

fn descriptio(Persona p) → string {
    return p.nomen
}

main {
    const Persona p ← Persona {nomen = "Marcus", aetas = 30}
    print descriptio(p)
}

Functions on a record

A genus can carry functions alongside its fields.

class Punctum {
    int x
    int y

    fn summa() → int {
        return self.x + self.y
    }
}

main {
    const Punctum p ← Punctum {x = 1, y = 2}
    print p.summa()
}

ego — "I" — is the receiver, what other languages spell this or self.
